title: Butkara Stupa
geometryBasis: Pakistan’s Department of Archaeology identifies Butkara I at 72.36793° E, 34.76573° N, within the named seven-vertex OSM precinct. The story coordinate identifies the separately mapped Saidu Sharif Monastery. Present ruin interpreted from factual text by the original excavator.
sectionBasis: Excavator Domenico Faccenna reports surviving concentric courses across five principal periods. The phase-IV lower base is 17.52 m across with a 3.25 m path. The top surviving phase-V course is 15.6 m across. The phase-I exposed core is 6 m across, best preserved to 4.70 m.
limitations: Official precinct coordinate is the best available anchor for the Great Stupa centre. Move the model only if a better survey identifies that centre.
The model shows the excavated remains. Adjacent votive base placements, localized collapse, individual masonry and peripheral annexes are representative estimates.
No intact historical dome or sculptures are reconstructed. Separate Saidu Sharif I is outside the model scope.
